items.stem: An owner wants to transfer the risk of uncertain excavation quantities on a project where ground conditions are poorly known. Which contract approach best fits?

options.text: A measured/unit-price arrangement so payment follows actual quantities
options.rationale: Correct: unit-price contracting suits uncertain quantities by paying for measured work.

options.text: A pure lump-sum contract with no remeasurement
options.rationale: A lump sum forces the contractor to price unknowns, inflating bids and inviting claims.

options.text: Refusing any contract until all quantities are known
options.rationale: Full certainty before contracting is rarely feasible and delays the project.

options.text: A handshake agreement to decide later

items.explanation: Correct: unit-price contracting suits uncertain quantities by paying for measured work.

items.stem: A contractor submits a delay claim. What evidence most strengthens a well-founded extension-of-time claim?

options.text: A baseline programme and records showing the delaying event's impact on the critical path
options.rationale: Correct: critical-path impact evidenced against a baseline supports a defensible delay claim.

options.text: A general assertion that the job 'felt slow'
options.rationale: Unsupported assertions do not substantiate a claim.
Desired margin is irrelevant to entitlement.
Good weather would not support a delay claim.

items.explanation: Correct: critical-path impact evidenced against a baseline supports a defensible delay claim.

items.stem: A design change arrives mid-construction. Which TWO steps are essential to proper change control? (Select TWO)

options.text: Documenting the change and its cost/time impact in a change order
options.rationale: Correct: changes must be documented with cost and schedule impact.
Correct: authorised approval is required before executing the change.

options.text: Starting the new work immediately on a verbal instruction
options.rationale: Acting on an undocumented verbal instruction undermines change control.

options.text: Hiding the change from the owner to avoid delay
options.rationale: Concealment is improper and creates disputes.

options.text: Assuming the subcontractor will absorb the cost silently

items.explanation: Correct: changes must be documented with cost and schedule impact. Correct: authorised approval is required before executing the change.
